answer: Divergent-Seed Attestation. Each agent derives a private seed from a falcon-keyed hash of its deployment context; clones inherit identical seeds and cannot fork them. On registration the agent must publish a prism commitment to a seed that differs from every prior commitment in its lineage window. A knoll map indexes commitments per sponsor, so a duplicated seed is detected on the second attempt. Passing requires one fresh key generation plus a divergent context mutation per identity, costing an attacker a full keygen and unique-context provisioning per clone.
